en: And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Yazid, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abi Layla, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib; (H) and Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr and 'Ubayd ibn Ya'ish narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Numayr: 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abi Layla, from 'Ali, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), similar to the hadith of al-Hakam from Ibn Abi Layla, and he added to the hadith: 'Ali said: "I never abandoned it since I heard it from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." It was said to him: "Not even on the night of Siffin?" He said: "Not even on the night of Siffin." And in the hadith of 'Ata' from Mujahid from Ibn Abi Layla, he said: I said to him: "Not even on the night of Siffin?"

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us: Waki' narrated to us; (H) and 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: My father narrated to us; (H) and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us; all of them from Shu'bah, with this chain of transmission, and in the hadith of Mu'adh: "when you both take your place of rest at night."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's—both narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, who said: I heard Ibn Abi Layla: 'Ali narrated to us that Fatimah complained of what she suffered from the hand-mill in her hand. Captives were brought to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), so she went to him but did not find him, and she met 'A'ishah and informed her. When the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) arrived, 'A'ishah informed him of Fatimah's visit to her. So the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came to us when we had already taken our places of rest. We were about to stand up, but the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Stay in your places." Then he sat between us until I felt the coolness of his foot on my chest. Then he said: "Shall I not teach you something better than what you asked for? When you take your places of rest, declare the greatness of Allah (say Allahu Akbar) thirty-four times, glorify Him (say Subhan Allah) thirty-three times, and praise Him (say Al-hamdulillah) thirty-three times; that is better for you both than a servant."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb, and Ishaq narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Bishr, from Mis'ar, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Rishdin, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Juwayriyah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) passed by her when he prayed the morning prayer, or after he prayed the morning prayer... and he mentioned similar to it, except that he said: "Subhan Allahi 'adada khalqihi, Subhan Allahi rida nafsihi, Subhan Allahi zinata 'arshihi, Subhan Allahi midada kalimatih" (Glory be to Allah according to the number of His creation; glory be to Allah according to His own good pleasure; glory be to Allah according to the weight of His Throne; glory be to Allah according to the ink of His words).

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, 'Amr al-Naqid, and Ibn Abi 'Umar—and the wording is Ibn Abi 'Umar's—narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, freed slave of the family of Talhah, from Kurayb, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Juwayriyah, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) went out from her early in the morning when he prayed the dawn prayer, while she was in her place of prayer. Then he returned after the forenoon had advanced while she was still sitting. He said: "Are you still in the same state in which I left you?" She said: "Yes." The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, I said four words three times after leaving you; if they were weighed against all that you have said since today, they would outweigh them: 'Subhan Allahi wa bihamdihi, 'adada khalqihi, wa rida nafsihi, wa zinata 'arshihi, wa midada kalimatih' (Glory be to Allah and with His praise, according to the number of His creation, according to His own good pleasure, according to the weight of His Throne, and according to the ink of His words)."

And Ibn Numayr narrated to us: 'Abdullah—meaning Ibn Idris—narrated to us: 'Asim ibn Kulayb informed us with this chain of transmission, saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to me: "Say: 'O Allah, indeed I ask You for guidance and correctness (al-huda wa al-sadad).'" Then he mentioned the like of it.

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard 'Asim ibn Kulayb, from Abu Burdah, from 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to me: "Say: 'O Allah, guide me and direct me rightly' (Allahumma-hdini wa saddidni); and keep in mind through 'guidance' your being guided along the path, and through 'rightness' the straight alignment of an arrow."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to say: "There is no god but Allah alone. He granted glory to His host, gave victory to His servant, and defeated the confederates alone, and there is nothing after Him."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Husayn ibn 'Ali narrated to us, from Za'idah, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ubaydullah, from Ibrahim ibn Suwayd, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from 'Abdullah, who said: When evening came, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to say: "We have entered the evening and dominion belongs to Allah, and all praise is for Allah; there is no god but Allah alone, having no partner. O Allah, I ask You of the good of this night and the good of what is in it, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of what is in it. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from laziness, decrepitude, the evils of old age, the trial of this world, and the torment of the grave." Al-Hasan ibn 'Ubaydullah said: And Zubayd added to me in it, from Ibrahim ibn Suwayd, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from 'Abdullah, attributing it to the Prophet, that he said: "There is no god but Allah alone, having no partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things competent."

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ubaydullah, from Ibrahim ibn Suwayd, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from 'Abdullah, who said: When evening came, the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to say: "We have entered the evening and dominion belongs to Allah, and all praise is for Allah; there is no god but Allah alone, having no partner." He said: I think he said among them: "His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things competent. My Lord, I ask You for the good of what is in this night and the good of what follows it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of what is in this night and the evil of what follows it. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and the evils of old age. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from torment in the Fire and torment in the grave." And when morning came, he would also say that: "We have entered the morning and dominion belongs to Allah."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ubaydullah: Ibrahim ibn Suwayd al-Nakha'i narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: When evening came, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to say: "We have entered the evening and dominion belongs to Allah, and all praise is for Allah; there is no god but Allah alone, having no partner." Al-Hasan said: Then al-Zubayd narrated to me that he memorized from Ibrahim concerning this: "His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things competent. O Allah, I ask You for the good of this night, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of this night and the evil of what follows it. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from laziness and the evils of old age. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from torment in the Fire and torment in the grave."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr—and the wording is Ibn Numayr's—narrated to us; Ishaq said: He informed us, and the other two said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from 'Asim, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith, and from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: I do not say to you except as the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to say; he used to say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from incapacity, laziness, cowardice, miserliness, decrepitude, and the torment of the grave. O Allah, grant my soul its piety and purify it; You are the best of those who purify it, You are its Guardian and its Master. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from knowledge that does not benefit, from a heart that is not humble, from a soul that is never satisfied, and from a supplication that is not answered."

And Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq with this chain of transmission, the like of it, except that Ibn al-Muthanna said in his narration: "and chastity" (al-'iffah).

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar both narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abdullah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he used to say: "O Allah, I ask You for guidance, piety, chastity, and self-sufficiency" (Allahumma inni as'aluka al-huda wa al-tuqa wa al-'afaf wa al-ghina).

Ibrahim ibn Dinar narrated to us: Abu Qatan 'Amr ibn al-Haytham al-Quta'i narrated to us, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Salamah al-Majishun, from Qudamah ibn Musa, from Abu Salih al-Samman, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to say: "O Allah, set right for me my religion, which is the safeguard of my affair; and set right for me my worldly life, wherein is my livelihood; and set right for me my Hereafter, to which is my return; and make life an increase for me in every good, and make death a relief for me from every evil."
And Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated it to us: 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Sabbah al-Misma'i narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us in this chain of transmission.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa al-Ash'ari, from his father, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he used to supplicate with this supplication: "O Allah, forgive me my wrongdoing, my ignorance, my excess in my affair, and that which You know better than me. O Allah, forgive me my seriousness, my joking, my unintentional mistakes, and my intentional deeds, and all of that is in me. O Allah, forgive me what I have sent forth and what I have held back, what I have kept secret and what I have proclaimed, and that which You know better than me; You are the One Who brings forward, and You are the One Who defers, and You are over all things competent."

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: Sulayman ibn Bilal informed me, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that whenever the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was on a journey and reached the end of the night, he would say: "May a hearer hear [our] praise of Allah and His fine trial upon us. Our Lord, accompany us and favor us, seeking refuge in Allah from the Fire."

Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated to me: 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr Abu Ma'mar narrated to us: 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us: Al-Husayn narrated to us: Ibn Buraydah narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Ya'mar, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to say: "O Allah, to You I have surrendered, in You I have believed, upon You I have relied, to You I have turned in repentance, and by Your help I have disputed. O Allah, I seek refuge in Your Might—there is no god but You—lest You lead me astray. You are the Living Who does not die, while jinn and humans die."

And 'Abdullah ibn Hashim narrated to me: Waki' narrated to us, from al-Awza'i, from 'Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, from Farwah ibn Nawfal, from 'A'ishah, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to say in his supplication: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done and the evil of what I have not done."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Jabalah narrated to us: Muhammad—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us; both from Shu'bah, from Husayn, with this chain of transmission, the like of it, except that in the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ja'far it is: "and from the evil of what I have not done."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb both narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to us, from Husayn, from Hilal, from Farwah ibn Nawfal, who said: I asked 'A'ishah about a supplication with which the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to supplicate, and she said: He used to say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done and the evil of what I have not done."

Yahya ibn Yahya and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim—and the wording is Yahya's—both narrated to us: Jarir informed us, from Mansur, from Hilal, from Farwah ibn Nawfal al-Ashja'i, who said: I asked 'A'ishah about what the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to supplicate Allah with, and she said: He used to say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done and from the evil of what I have not done."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Anas, that whenever the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) retired to his bed, he would say: "All praise is for Allah Who fed us, gave us drink, sufficed us, and gave us shelter; for how many are there who have neither one to suffice them nor one to shelter them."

And Abu Kurayb narrated to us: 'Abdah narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar with this chain of transmission, and he said: "then let him say: 'In Your name, my Lord, I have laid down my side; so if You preserve my soul alive, have mercy upon it.'"

And Ishaq ibn Musa al-Ansari narrated to us: Anas ibn 'Iyad narrated to us: 'Ubaydullah narrated to us: Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi narrated to me, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When one of you retires to his bed, let him take the inner edge of his lower garment and dust his bed with it, and let him pronounce the name of Allah, for he does not know what succeeded him upon his bed after him. Then, when he wishes to lie down, let him lie down on his right side and say: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, my Lord; by You I have laid down my side and by You I raise it up. If You take my soul, forgive it; and if You release it, preserve it with that wherewith You preserve Your righteous servants.'"

And Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb both narrated to us: Ibn Abi 'Ubaydah narrated to us: My father narrated to us; both from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Fatimah came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) asking him for a servant, so he said to her: "Say: 'O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens...'" similar to the hadith of Suhayl from his father.

And 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan al-Wasiti narrated to me: Khalid—meaning al-Tahhan—narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to command us, when we took our places of rest, to say... similar to the hadith of Jarir, and he said: "from the evil of every living creature whose forelock You take hold of."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us, from Suhayl, who said: Abu Salih used to command us, when one of us wished to sleep, to lie down on his right side and then say: "O Allah, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth and Lord of the magnificent Throne, our Lord and Lord of all things, Cleaver of the grain and date stone, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel, and the Furqan (the Criterion/Quran): I seek refuge in You from the evil of everything whose forelock You take hold of. O Allah, You are the First, and there is nothing before You; and You are the Last, and there is nothing after You; and You are the Manifest, and there is nothing above You; and You are the Hidden, and there is nothing beneath You. Settle the debt for us and enrich us against poverty." And he used to relate that from Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).

'Uqbah ibn Mukram al-'Ammi and Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' both narrated to us: Ghundar narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Khalid, who said: I heard 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith narrating from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, that he commanded a man, when he took his place of rest, to say: "O Allah, You created my soul and You take it away; to You belongs its death and its life. If You keep it alive, preserve it; and if You cause it to die, forgive it. O Allah, I ask You for well-being." A man said to him: "Did you hear this from 'Umar?" He said: "From someone better than 'Umar—from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." Ibn Nafi' said in his narration: from 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith, and he did not mention: "I heard."
